maya: EDR alert on ALICE-LAPTOP-2 — msiexec spawned kernel driver load, driver was signed by 'QuickInstall Ltd' (unfamiliar). EDR quarantined the driver and isolated the host. sha256=3f5b9c8a2d4f1b7e9a6c4d2f3e8b9a1c2d3e4f5a6b7c8d9e0f1a2b3c4d5e6f7a :eyes:
edr-bot: [Automated] Detection ID DET-2141592653 | Action: quarantine_file, isolate_host | Host: ALICE-LAPTOP-2 | User: alice.r | Confidence: high
samir: Acknowledged. Is the host still on the network or fully isolated? Need hostname, IP, OS build and AD username.
maya: Hostname: ALICE-LAPTOP-2, IP: 10.40.12.77 (last seen), OS: Windows 11 22H2, AD: REDWOOD\\alice.r. Isolation: yes (network quarantine applied), agent heartbeat still up but no external access.
jordan: Can we get the process tree and the exact path of the quarantined driver? Also share the driver cert details (issuer, serial) if available.
maya: Process tree from EDR: System -> msiexec.exe (pid 1432) -> installhelper.exe (pid 1520) -> rundll32.exe (pid 1568) -> driverloader.sys attempted load. Quarantined path: C:\Windows\Temp\QuickInstall\driverloader.sys. Driver cert CN='QuickInstall Ltd', O='QuickInstall Ltd', Issuer='US-Software-Signing-CA' serial=0A3F9C...
samir: Good. Please collect forensic artifacts: 1) EDR full zip, 2) autoruns, 3) scheduled tasks, 4) driver file hash and binary. Use the secure collection command below and upload to secure bucket 'sec-collect/2141592653'. Do NOT transfer to personal cloud.

# collect EDR artifacts
edrctl collect --host ALICE-LAPTOP-2 --since 2h --artifacts processes,drivers,registry,network --out /tmp/edr-2141592653.zip
aws s3 cp /tmp/edr-2141592653.zip s3://sec-collect/2141592653 --sse aws:kms

jordan: Also run these local checks before shutting down the machine: list running services, `sc queryex`, `driverquery /v`, and export registry keys for HKLM\\SYSTEM\\CurrentControlSet\\Services\\driverloader and HKLM\\SOFTWARE\\Microsoft\\Windows\\CurrentVersion\\Run.
ella: I'm taking console access to the MDM now to run a full AV + deep EDR scan. I'll also check USB mount history and recent installer packages. Opening INC-2141 and assigning to samir for triage + escalation to infra if we find lateral attempts. @samir please confirm incident severity.
samir: Thanks @ella. Based on initial indicators (signed binary, kernel component, network beaconing attempt seen to 45.77.12.9 on port 443) mark as P1 until we rule out lateral movement. I'll grab packets from the host if available and check SIEM for related IPs.
edr-bot: Follow-up scan scheduled in 30m; results will post to this thread. If agent disconnects, SecOps will trigger remote wipe placeholder.
maya: Collected EDR packet capture shows TLS handshake to 45.77.12.9 and periodic small beacons. No successful exfil evidence yet. Action items: 1) Keep host isolated; 2) block cert thumbprint org-wide if vendor not approved; 3) create detection rule for msiexec spawning driver loads; 4) rotate any machine-scoped KMS keys if there was evidence of key access.
jordan: For post-incident: add playbook step to deny msiexec child processes starting driver installs (allowlist installers only), add RBAC check to ensure only SAs can push signed drivers. Also ensure audit logging captures driver loads (Event ID 6xx).
ella: Full AV + EDR deep scan completed — found additional dropped DLLs in AppData/Local/Temp, quarantined. Uploading collected artifacts now to s3://sec-collect/2141592653.
samir: I'll run yara on the binary and cross-check VirusTotal and internal intel. If malicious, we'll push vendor cert revocation and update Defender/EDR signatures.
maya: Postmortem note: rotate any service accounts that the installer touched, update onboarding docs to block unknown vendor driver installs, schedule follow-up meeting with Platform to review KMS access logs. Closing on status for now, will update after yara/VT results :thumbsup:
